heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Bangladesh
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to EOR & PEO in Bangladesh
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for EOR & PEO in Bangladesh.

steps.title: Contract Drafting & Compliance Review
steps.description: Drafting of the employment contract in accordance with the Bangladesh Labour Act 2006 (amended 2025). This includes defining the category of worker (Permanent, Probationary, Temporary) and ensuring all mandatory clauses like leave, working hours, and termination are included.

steps.title: Document Collection & Verification
steps.description: Collection of mandatory employee documents including National ID (NID), Passport-sized photographs, academic certificates, and previous employment clearance. Background checks (if requested) are conducted with explicit employee consent.

steps.title: Tax & Social Security Registration
steps.description: Registration of the employee with the National Board of Revenue (NBR) for an Electronic Tax Identification Number (e-TIN). Creation of records for the Workers' Profit Participation Fund (WPPF) and Gratuity/Provident Fund where applicable.

steps.title: Payroll Setup & Bank Account Linking
steps.description: Setting up the employee in the payroll system, ensuring bank account details are linked for salary disbursement via EFT (Electronic Fund Transfer) or Bank Transfer as per local regulations.

steps.title: Equipment & IT Provisioning
steps.description: Coordination of assets such as laptops, work-from-home stipends (where applicable), and secure IT access setup to ensure the employee is ready for day one.

items.title: Permanent Establishment Risk
items.text: Hiring remote workers for durations exceeding 183 days without a local entity can trigger PE risk. An EOR mitigates this by becoming the legal employer of record, but strategic advisory is recommended for long-term setups.

items.title: Probation Period Limits
items.text: Under the Labour Act, the probation period for a clerk is maximum 6 months, and for others, it is 3 months. During this period, termination is simplified with shorter notice.

items.title: Social Security & Benefits
items.text: While Bangladesh doesn't have a universal social security tax like Europe, mandatory Gratuity (after 1 year) and Provident Fund (if company policy exists) are the primary long-term benefits for employees.

items.title: Termination Rigidity
items.text: Terminating permanent employees is difficult after the probation period. It requires valid cause (misconduct, retrenchment) and adherence to strict compensation rules (30 days' notice or pay in lieu).

items.title: Festival Bonuses (Eid Bonuses)
items.text: It is customary and legally expected to provide two festival bonuses (usually during Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha) equivalent to one month's basic salary each.

items.title: Work Week Structure
items.text: The standard work week is Sunday to Thursday, with Friday and Saturday as weekends. Standard working hours are 48 hours per week (8 hours/day).

items.title: Mobile Banking Popularity
items.text: Many employees prefer salary disbursement or expense reimbursements via mobile financial services like bKash or Nagad for immediate access to funds.

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors through an EOR in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Yes, EOR providers can facilitate both full-time employment and professional contractor agreements, ensuring the right classification to avoid legal disputes.

faqs.question: What is the typical notice period for resignation?
faqs.answer: For permanent monthly-rated workers, the statutory resignation notice period is 60 days. However, employers can agree to shorter periods in the contract.

faqs.question: Is health insurance mandatory for EOR employees?
faqs.answer: While not statutory under the Labour Act, providing private medical insurance is a highly competitive benefit in the Bangladesh tech and corporate sectors.

faqs.question: What is the WPPF?
faqs.answer: The Workers' Profit Participation Fund is mandatory for companies meeting specific financial thresholds, requiring 5% of net profit to be distributed among eligible employees.

faqs.question: Can we pay in USD?
faqs.answer: Local employees must be paid in BDT as per Bangladesh Bank regulations. Cross-border payments in USD are restricted for resident employees.

faqs.question: Who handles the taxes for the employee?
faqs.answer: The EOR provider calculates, withholds, and remits personal income tax (PAYE) to the NBR on behalf of the employee.

steps.title: Data Gathering & Attendance Sync
steps.description: Consolidation of monthly attendance data, overtime records, and leave applications. In Bangladesh, many firms sync this by the 25th of each month.

steps.title: Tax & Deduction Calculation
steps.description: Applying income tax slabs (progressive rates) and mandatory deductions such as Provident Fund (if applicable) and professional tax. Ensuring calculations align with the Finance Act 2024-25.

steps.title: Review & Approval
steps.description: Internal or client review of the payroll register. Highlighting any deviations like mid-month joiners or exit settlements (gratuity, notice pay).

steps.title: Bank Transfer & Fund Disbursement
steps.description: Generation of bank files for electronic transfer. Employees typically expect salaries by the 1st to 7th of the following month.

steps.title: Payslip Distribution & Statutory Filing
steps.description: Sending digital payslips to employees and preparing monthly tax withholding reports for the National Board of Revenue (NBR).

items.title: Electronic Payment Mandate
items.text: For companies with a significant workforce, salary payments exceeding BDT 15,000 should ideally be made through bank transfers to maintain a clear audit trail and compliance with NBR requirements.

items.title: Festival Bonus Timing
items.text: Failure to pay festival bonuses (usually two per year) according to the company policy and custom can lead to industrial relations issues and legal penalties.

items.title: Investment Tax Credit
items.text: Employees can claim a tax rebate for specific investments (DPS, Savings Bonds, Insurance). Payroll providers should collect documents in Q4 to adjust tax withholdings.

items.title: Gratuity Entitlement
items.text: Employees who have completed 1 year of service are entitled to gratuity upon termination or resignation, calculated as 30 days' basic wages for each year of service.

items.title: Annual Leave Encashment
items.text: Under the Labour Act, employees can carry forward leave, and upon exit, any unused annual leave must be encashed.

items.title: Provident Fund (PF)
items.text: While not mandatory for all sectors, if a PF is established, the employer and employee typically contribute 10% of the basic salary each.

faqs.question: Are there different tax-free thresholds for women or elderly?
faqs.answer: Yes, for women and taxpayers aged 65+, the tax-free limit is BDT 400,000. For physically challenged persons, it is BDT 475,000.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late tax filing?
faqs.answer: Late filing or non-filing of monthly withholding returns can result in penalties and interest charges from the NBR.

faqs.question: Can salaries be paid in foreign currency?
faqs.answer: Generally, for local employees, salaries must be paid in BDT. Foreigners with valid work permits may have specific repatriation rights through authorized dealer banks.

steps.title: Gross Salary Input
steps.description: Defining the total monthly remuneration which includes Basic Salary, House Rent, Medical Allowance, and Conveyance.

steps.title: Taxable Income Derivation
steps.description: Applying tax exemptions (e.g., House rent is exempt up to 50% of basic or BDT 25,000 per month). Calculating the net taxable monthly income.

steps.title: Progressive Tax Application
steps.description: Applying the latest slabs (0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%) as per the Finance Act 2024-25 to determine the monthly tax withholding (PAYE).

steps.title: Net Take-Home Calculation
steps.description: Subtracting tax and other mandatory deductions (like PF) from the Gross Salary to provide the final Net Take-Home amount.

items.title: Standard Tax Threshold
items.text: This calculator assumes the general tax-free threshold of BDT 350,000. For female/elderly taxpayers, the results should be adjusted manually.

items.title: Investment Rebatable
items.text: The calculator provides a baseline PAYE figure and does not account for potential tax rebates from personal investments or CSR contributions.

faqs.question: Does this include festival bonuses?
faqs.answer: The calculator usually focuses on monthly recurring pay. One-off festival bonuses should be calculated separately as they are taxed at the same progressive rates.

faqs.question: Is Provident Fund mandatory in the calculation?
faqs.answer: PF is only included if configured as a benefit by the employer. It typically involves a 10% deduction from the Basic salary.

items.title: Festival Bonus Budgeting
items.text: Remember that net pay calculators focus on monthly income. Annual budgeting must include two festival bonuses which are mandatory for most employees.

items.title: Tax Rebate Opportunity
items.text: Employees can claim up to 15% tax rebate on eligible investments (like DPS or stocks), which can increase the monthly net take-home significantly.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Bangladesh
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Incorporation in Bangladesh
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Incorporation in Bangladesh.

steps.title: Name Clearance
steps.description: Apply for name clearance via the RJSC (Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms) portal. Usually processed in 1-2 business days. Fee is approx BDT 230-600.

steps.title: Bank Account Opening & Capital Remittance
steps.description: For foreign-owned companies, opening a temporary bank account to remit paid-up capital is required. An encashment certificate from the bank is a mandatory document for registration.

steps.title: Documentation & Stamp Duty
steps.description: Drafting Memorandum of Association (MoA) and Articles of Association (AoA). Payment of stamp duty (ranges from BDT 2,000 to 10,000 depending on capital) and registration fees.

steps.title: RJSC Registration & Incorporation Certificate
steps.description: Submission of all documents to RJSC. Upon approval, the Certificate of Incorporation, Form XII (Director list), and certified MoA/AoA are issued.

steps.title: Post-Incorporation Licensing
steps.description: Applying for Trade License (City Corporation), e-TIN (NBR), and VAT registration. Depending on the industry, IRC/ERC or Factory License may be required.

items.title: Private Limited Company
items.text: The most common vehicle for foreign investors, allowing 100% foreign ownership in most sectors. Requires minimum 2 directors and 2 shareholders.

items.title: Branch vs Liaison Office
items.text: Liaison offices are strictly for non-revenue generating activities (marketing, coordination). If you intend to sell services or products locally, a Branch Office or Ltd Company is required.

items.title: BIDA Registration
items.text: Registering with the Bangladesh Investment Development Authority (BIDA) is essential for facilitating work permits, profit repatriation, and various tax incentives.

items.title: Director Residency
items.text: There is no strict residency requirement for directors in a Private Limited company, but at least one director must be a natural person.

items.title: Annual Filing Deadlines
items.text: Companies must hold an Annual General Meeting (AGM) and file annual returns (Schedule X) with RJSC within 30 days of the AGM.

faqs.question: Can a foreign individual be a sole director?
faqs.answer: No, a Bangladesh Private Limited company requires a minimum of two directors.

faqs.question: What is the minimum paid-up capital?
faqs.answer: Technically BDT 1, but for practical banking and work permit purposes, a minimum of USD 50,000 is often recommended for foreign-owned entities.

faqs.question: Can I register a company remotely?
faqs.answer: Most of the RJSC process is online, but certain documents require physical signatures/notarization, and bank account opening usually requires physical presence or legalized Power of Attorney.

heroData.title: Staffing in Bangladesh
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Staffing in Bangladesh
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Staffing in Bangladesh.

steps.title: Job Specification & Localization
steps.description: Defining roles and aligning salary expectations with the local Bangladesh market (Dhaka/Chittagong rates). Translating requirements if necessary for specific vocational roles.

steps.title: Sourcing via Portals & Networks
steps.description: Utilizing major portals like bdjobs.com, LinkedIn, and local niche groups. For executive roles, engaging with specialized search firms is common.

steps.title: Technical & Cultural Assessment
steps.description: Multi-stage interviews including technical tests (especially for IT roles) and cultural fit assessments to ensure alignment with global team dynamics.

steps.title: Reference & Background Checks
steps.description: Verifying academic credentials through university portals and conducting employment reference checks. This is a critical step in the Bangladesh hiring market.

steps.title: Offer Management & Onboarding
steps.description: Negotiating the 'Gross vs Basic' salary structure and preparing the offer letter. Coordinating with the EOR provider for contract signing.

items.title: Tech Talent Hotspots
items.text: Dhaka's Banani, Gulshan, and Uttara areas are hubs for software developers and IT professionals. The talent pool is growing rapidly in AI and Full-stack development.

items.title: Salary Expectations
items.text: Salaries for tech roles have seen a 15-20% YoY increase. Competitive benefits like insurance and flexible work are becoming standard requirements for top tier talent.

items.title: Notice Period Negotiation
items.text: Top candidates often have 2-3 month notice periods. Strategic 'notice buyout' options are sometimes used to accelerate urgent hires.

items.title: Educational Prestige
items.text: Graduates from top public universities (DU, BUET) and leading private universities (NSU, BRAC) are highly sought after by multinational employers.

items.title: English Proficiency
items.text: The corporate workforce in Bangladesh generally has high English proficiency, especially in global-facing sectors like IT and Apparel.

items.title: Remote Work Trends
items.text: Dhaka's infrastructure is now capable of supporting high-end remote work; companies offering hybrid models see 40% higher retention among software engineers.

items.title: Upskilling Boom
items.text: Government initiatives like 'Digital Bangladesh' have created a massive pool of 600,000+ freelance and gig workers, many of whom are now transitioning to full-time remote roles.

items.title: Benefit Preferences
items.text: Beyond salary, the most requested benefits in BD are festival bonuses (2 per year), health insurance for family, and performance-based increments.

faqs.question: What is the typical probation period?
faqs.answer: As per the Bangladesh Labor Act, the standard probation period is 3 months for clerical roles and 6 months for professional/skilled roles.

faqs.question: Is employee insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: Group insurance is mandatory for establishments with 100 or more permanent workers. For smaller firms, it is an optional but recommended benefit.

faqs.question: Can we hire employees on fixed-term contracts?
faqs.answer: Yes, 'Badli' or casual workers can be hired on a fixed-term basis, but they are entitled to certain benefits if the term exceeds specific durations defined in the Labor Act.

heroData.title: HRIS in Bangladesh
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to HRIS in Bangladesh
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for HRIS in Bangladesh.

steps.title: Requirement Mapping
steps.description: Identifying local needs such as Bangladesh-specific tax slabs, festival bonus modules, and local bank integration for EFT.

steps.title: Data Migration & Cleaning
steps.description: Migrating employee master data from legacy systems or spreadsheets into the new HRIS, ensuring NID and e-TIN details are accurate.

steps.title: Configuration & Workflow Setup
steps.description: Setting up approval workflows for leave, expense claims, and daily attendance tracking (Geofencing vs Biometric integration).

steps.title: UAT & Employee Training
steps.description: Conducting User Acceptance Testing with the HR team and providing training sessions/manuals for the Self-Service Portal (ESS).

steps.title: Go-Live & Support
steps.description: Official launch of the platform. Ongoing support for troubleshooting and monthly payroll execution via the HRIS.

items.title: Data Privacy Considerations
items.text: While Bangladesh is developing its Data Protection Act, ensure your HRIS provider hosts data securely and complies with global standards like GDPR if handling expat data.

items.title: Mobile App Accessibility
items.text: High smartphone penetration means a mobile-first HRIS is essential for frontline employees to mark attendance and view payslips.

items.title: Tax Regulation Updates
items.text: Choose a vendor that provides timely updates to the Bangladesh tax engine, especially when the National Budget is announced in June.

items.title: Employee Self-Service (ESS)
items.text: Promoting ESS significantly reduces the burden on HR teams for managing leaves and document requests, which is increasingly expected by Gen-Z talent.

items.title: Biometric Integration
items.text: For manufacturing operations, integrating your HRIS with biometric attendance systems is a standard compliance requirement to track overtime accurately.

items.title: Bengali Language Support
items.text: Ensure your HRIS provides some level of Bengali interface or report generation for non-English speaking staff in satellite offices.

faqs.question: Is cloud-based data storage legal for HR?
faqs.answer: Yes, cloud storage is legal and widely used, provided it adheres to standard data privacy practices and is protected against unauthorized access.

faqs.question: Can global HRIS platforms handle BD tax?
faqs.answer: Most premium global platforms like Deel or Remote have localized engines for Bangladesh. For others, a third-party payroll provider may be needed to bridge the gap.

sections.title: Future of HR Tech in BD

items.title: AI in HR
items.text: Large enterprises in Bangladesh are starting to pilot AI-driven resume screening and engagement bots to manage high-volume recruitment cycles.

items.title: Financial Inclusion
items.text: Integrating HRIS with MFS (Mobile Financial Services) like bKash or Nagad is becoming critical for paying blue-collar workers and managing remote staff reimbursements.

heroData.title: Accounting in Bangladesh
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Accounting in Bangladesh
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Accounting in Bangladesh.

steps.title: Monthly Bookkeeping
steps.description: Maintaining ledger accounts, categorizing expenses, and reconciling bank statements as per IFRS/IAS adopted in Bangladesh.

steps.title: Statutory Audit Preparation
steps.description: Engaging a CA (Chartered Accountant) firm for the annual audit. Ensuring all supporting vouchers and contracts are organized for review.

steps.title: Financial Statement Finalization
steps.description: Drafting the Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss Statement, and Cash Flow Statement. Getting director approval and auditor sign-off.

steps.title: Tax Return Filing
steps.description: Using audited financials to prepare and file the Corporate Income Tax return (Form-24) with the NBR by the deadline (usually Jan 15th for June-end companies).

items.title: IFRS Convergence
items.text: Bangladesh has fully adopted IFRS for Public Interest Entities (PIEs). Smaller entities can use IFRS for SMEs.

items.title: Document Retention
items.text: Under the Companies Act and Tax laws, financial records and vouchers must be retained for at least 6-8 years for potential scrutiny.

items.title: Chartered Accountant Selection
items.text: Only firms registered with the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Bangladesh (ICAB) are authorized to sign off on statutory audits.

items.title: Document Language
items.text: While internal records can be in Bengali, the audited financial statements submitted to the RJSC must be in English for international consistency.

items.title: VAT Audit Scrutiny
items.text: Ensure all Mushak-6.3 tax invoices are properly filed and cross-referenced; VAT authorities often conduct spot audits on high-turnover businesses.

faqs.question: What is the standard financial year?
faqs.answer: The standard financial year in Bangladesh runs from 1st July to 30th June. Specialized sectors like Banking and Insurance may have different cycles.

faqs.question: Can we use global accounting software?
faqs.answer: Yes, standard platforms like Xero and Oracle are used, but they must be configured to generate local tax and VAT reports that comply with NBR formats.

steps.title: Trade License Renewal
steps.description: Applying for the annual renewal of the local Trade License from the respective City Corporation or Union Parishad. Required for all businesses by July each year.

steps.title: BIDA & IRC/ERC Compliance
steps.description: For firms involved in import/export, ensuring the Renewal of Import Registration Certificate (IRC) and Export Registration Certificate (ERC). Updating the BIDA registration with the latest investment data.

steps.title: Factory & Environmental Licensing
steps.description: If operating a manufacturing or IT park facility, ensuring the Factory License and Environmental Clearance Certificates are up to date with the latest DIFE guidelines.

steps.title: Annual Statutory Reporting
steps.description: Filing the mandatory Annual Returns (Schedule X) with the RJSC and ensuring the company secretary maintains the minutes of the AGM and Board meetings.

items.title: Trade License Penalties
items.text: Operating without a valid trade license can result in hefty penalties from the City Corporation and potential closure of business premises during inspections.

items.title: IRC/ERC Categories
items.text: Import/Export licenses are categorized based on value limits. Choosing the right category during the initial application is crucial for smooth customs clearance.

items.title: BIDA One-Stop Service (OSS)
items.text: Utilize the BIDA OSS portal for streamlined applications for work permits, utility connections, and various regulatory approvals.

items.title: Fire License Importance
items.text: A valid Fire Safety License is a prerequisite for most other license renewals and is strictly enforced for all commercial premises in Dhaka.

items.title: Trade License Jurisdiction
items.text: Ensure your Trade License is issued by the specific City Corporation (e.g., DNCC or DSCC) where your physical office is located.

faqs.question: What happens if we miss the CSR quota?
faqs.answer: While CSR is encouraged through tax rebates, there is currently no mandatory legal penalty for not meeting CSR targets for private firms.

faqs.question: How often are factory inspections?
faqs.answer: The DIFE conducts inspections at least once a year, focusing on safety, sanitation, and adherence to minimum wage regulations.

steps.title: e-TIN & VAT Registration
steps.description: Obtaining the 12-digit Electronic Tax Identification Number and the Business Identification Number (BIN) for VAT purposes.

steps.title: VAT Reporting & Returns
steps.description: Filing monthly VAT returns (Mushak 9.1) by the 15th of the following month, even for nil transactions.

steps.title: TDS (Tax Deducted at Source)
steps.description: Deducting tax from payments (salaries, local suppliers) at prescribed rates and depositing it to the treasury via Challan.

steps.title: Annual Tax Return Filing
steps.description: Submitting the comprehensive corporate tax return by the 'Tax Day' (usually 15th January for the previous July-June cycle).

items.title: Tax Holiday for Software
items.text: Bangladesh has traditionally offered tax holidays for IT enabled services (ITES). Always check the latest Finance Act for extensions or changes in eligibility.

items.title: Cash Payment Restrictions
items.text: Expenses exceeding BDT 500k per individual or BDT 3.6M per year must be paid via bank transfer to be tax-deductible.

items.title: Cashless Transaction Bonus
items.text: The NBR often provides a 2.5% reduction in the corporate tax rate for companies that maintain 100% of their transactions through banking channels.

items.title: Double Taxation Treaties
items.text: Bangladesh has DTAA treaties with over 30 countries including the US, UK, and Singapore, which can significantly reduce withholding taxes on dividends and royalties.

faqs.question: What is the corporate tax deadline?
faqs.answer: For companies with a June year-end, the deadline is generally 15th January of the following year. Penalties apply for late filing without prior approval.

faqs.question: Is VAT registration mandatory for all?
faqs.answer: Registration is mandatory if the annual turnover exceeds BDT 30 million. However, most service providers prefer voluntary registration to claim input tax credits.

heroData.title: MSA & Legal in Bangladesh
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to MSA & Legal in Bangladesh
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for MSA & Legal in Bangladesh.

steps.title: Drafting & Clause Alignment
steps.description: Preparing the Master Service Agreement (MSA) with specific focus on Indemnification, Intellectual Property (IP) rights, and Liability limits as per the Contract Act 1872.

steps.title: Expert Legal Review
steps.description: Engaging local counsel to ensure the agreement is enforceable under Bangladesh law and doesn't conflict with sector-specific regulations (e.g., Telecom or Banking).

steps.title: Dispute Resolution Strategy
steps.description: Defining the arbitration seat and governing law. Most international MSAs in Bangladesh opt for the Arbitration Act 2001 or SIAC (Singapore) for neutral adjudication.

steps.title: Execution & Stamp Duty
steps.description: Signing the agreement and ensuring it is properly stamped as per the Stamp Act 1899. Failure to pay stamp duty can make the document inadmissible in court.

items.title: IP Protection Nuances
items.text: Explicitly define 'Work for Hire' clauses in your MSA to ensure all Intellectual Property created by local contractors or employees is transferred to the global parent entity.

items.title: Arbitration over Litigation
items.text: Given the backlog in the traditional court system, always include a robust Arbitration clause (citing the Arbitration Act 2001) for faster dispute resolution.

items.title: Stamp Duty Compliance
items.text: Under the Stamp Act, all B2B contracts must be printed on non-judicial stamp paper of appropriate value to be legally enforceable.

items.title: Notarization Requirements
items.text: For added legal weight, especially in cross-border MSAs, having the agreement notarized by a local Notary Public is highly recommended.

faqs.question: Are electronic signatures legally recognized?
faqs.answer: The ICT Act 2006 recognizes digital signatures, but many traditional banks and some government departments still prefer physical signatures and seals.

faqs.question: What is the standard limitation of liability?
faqs.answer: While it varies, many MSAs in Bangladesh cap liability at the total value of fees paid over the previous 12 months, though this is subject to negotiation.

heroData.title: Software in Bangladesh
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Software in Bangladesh
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Software in Bangladesh.

steps.title: Discovery & Technical Scoping
steps.description: Collaborating with Bangladesh-based tech teams to define the tech stack (React, Node, Python) and architectural requirements.

steps.title: Agile Development Sprints
steps.description: Implementing two-week sprints with regular Jira updates and daily stand-ups to ensure alignment with global product goals.

steps.title: QA & Automated Testing
steps.description: Rigorous testing phases including Unit tests, Integration tests, and User Acceptance Testing (UAT). Utilizing CI/CD pipelines for deployment.

steps.title: Deployment & Maintenance
steps.description: Go-live on cloud infrastructure (AWS/Azure) and providing ongoing L1/L2 support for the software application.

items.title: Time Zone Advantage
items.text: Bangladesh (GMT+6) provides a significant overlap with European markets and a perfect 'follow-the-sun' model for US-based support/maintenance.

items.title: Emerging AI Hub
items.text: Dhaka is seeing a surge in AI-focused startups and specialized LLM fine-tuning service providers, making it a competitive market for high-end tech talent.

items.title: BASIS Membership
items.text: Partnering with BASIS-member companies ensures you are working with verified entities that adhere to a standard code of conduct in the local tech sector.

items.title: Infrastructure Resilience
items.text: Most professional tech parks and premium offices in Dhaka have dual ISP connections and dedicated power backups (IPS/UPS) to ensure 99.9% uptime.

faqs.question: Is IP ownership guaranteed?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the contract explicitly states that all work-product belongs to the client. Bangladesh laws respect Intellectual Property transfer clauses.

faqs.question: What is the typical team size available?
faqs.answer: Providers can scale from a single dedicated developer to a full squad of 10-15 members including QA and PMs within 2-4 weeks notice.

heroData.title: Marketing in Bangladesh
heroData.subtitle: Comprehensive guide to Marketing in Bangladesh
heroData.description: Detailed insights and providers for Marketing in Bangladesh.

steps.title: Market Research & Persona Building
steps.description: Identifying local consumer behaviors, preferred social platforms (Facebook is dominant in BD), and linguistic nuances (Banglish vs Formal Bangla).

steps.title: Content Creation & Localization
steps.description: Developing localized creative assets including video content, social media posts, and blog articles tailored to the Bangladesh audience.

steps.title: Multi-Channel Distribution
steps.description: Executing paid ad campaigns on Facebook, Google, and local ad networks. Influencer marketing is also highly effective for youth-centric brands.

steps.title: Performance Tracking & Optimization
steps.description: Monitoring CPC, CPM, and Conversion rates. Adjusting campaign budgets based on real-time ROI data from the local market.

items.title: Facebook First Strategy
items.text: Over 50 million active users in Bangladesh make Facebook the primary channel for B2C and even some B2B marketing initiatives.

items.title: Linguistic Nuances
items.text: While formal Bangla is used for official branding, 'Banglish' (Romanized Bangla with English mix) is highly effective for social media engagement with the Gen-Z and Millennial demographics.

items.title: Video Content Dominance
items.text: Video outperforms static imagery by 3x in Bangladesh. Investing in localized video content for Facebook and TikTok is essential for reach.

items.title: Micro-Influencer Strategy
items.text: In Dhaka, micro-influencers with engaged niche followings often provide better ROI than celebrity endorsements for high-consideration tech products.

faqs.question: How are Facebook ad spends managed?
faqs.answer: Most agencies use international cards for USD payments. Be aware of the 15% VAT on digital ad spend imposed by the National Board of Revenue.

faqs.question: Can agencies support outdoor (OOH) marketing?
faqs.answer: Yes, many full-service agencies manage billboard placements in high-traffic areas like Banani, Airport Road, and Pragati Sarani.
